routeFamilies.name: Seattle round trip with Glacier Bay
routeFamilies.why: Fly nonstop to Seattle and sail into Glacier Bay National Park, where park rangers come aboard for the day. Only Princess, Holland America and Norwegian hold the permits, so this is the route to pick if Glacier Bay itself matters.
routeFamilies.tradeoff: Usually the priciest Seattle round trip, and the open-ocean run past Vancouver Island means two sea days.
routeFamilies.bestFor: The full glacier day without changing airports
routeFamilies.textBasis: Planner summary written in P6 from the catalog and line notes; general knowledge, not a sourced figure.

routeFamilies.name: Seattle round trip with Endicott Arm & Dawes Glacier
routeFamilies.why: The most sailings and lines from Seattle. The glacier day is Endicott Arm, a narrow fjord ending at Dawes Glacier with steep walls close on both sides.
routeFamilies.tradeoff: Floating ice can stop big ships short of the glacier face; the captain may turn back early or go elsewhere.
routeFamilies.bestFor: Most choice of ships and dates from Seattle
routeFamilies.textBasis: Planner summary written in P6 from the catalog and line notes; general knowledge, not a sourced figure.

routeFamilies.name: Seattle round trip with Tracy Arm
routeFamilies.why: Carnival and MSC sailings, often the lowest fares from Seattle. The glacier day is Tracy Arm, a long fjord with waterfalls and twin glaciers.
routeFamilies.tradeoff: Large ships often cannot get close to the glacier faces in Tracy Arm, so the scenery is the fjord more than the ice.
routeFamilies.textBasis: Planner summary written in P6 from the catalog and line notes; general knowledge, not a sourced figure.

routeFamilies.name: Seattle round trip with Hubbard Glacier
routeFamilies.why: A single Norwegian sailing that reaches Hubbard Glacier, one of the largest tidewater glaciers in North America, far up the Gulf of Alaska coast.
routeFamilies.tradeoff: Only one date in the window, and getting to Hubbard and back costs extra time at sea.
routeFamilies.bestFor: A huge glacier face from Seattle
routeFamilies.textBasis: Planner summary written in P6 from the catalog and line notes; general knowledge, not a sourced figure.

routeFamilies.name: Seattle round trip, no glacier day
routeFamilies.why: A smaller, upscale ship with port calls but no scheduled glacier cruising.
routeFamilies.tradeoff: Skips the glacier day that most families come for.
routeFamilies.bestFor: A quieter ship, if glaciers are not the point
routeFamilies.textBasis: Planner summary written in P6 from the catalog and line notes; general knowledge, not a sourced figure.

routeFamilies.name: Vancouver round trip
routeFamilies.why: Starts in Vancouver and sails north through the sheltered Inside Passage, so more of the trip is calm, scenic water instead of open ocean. Glacier days vary by ship: Glacier Bay, Dawes, Tracy Arm, Hubbard or the Stikine Icecap.
routeFamilies.tradeoff: No nonstop flight from Albuquerque to Vancouver, and a Canada border crossing at the start and end (passports needed).
routeFamilies.textBasis: Planner summary written in P6 from the catalog and line notes; general knowledge, not a sourced figure.

routeFamilies.name: One way Vancouver to Seward/Whittier
routeFamilies.why: Ends in Seward or Whittier near Anchorage, so no days are spent sailing back south. Many add a second glacier day such as College Fjord or Hubbard Glacier, and you can add Denali or Anchorage time before flying home.
routeFamilies.tradeoff: Fly into one city and home from another, plus a 2 to 3 hour transfer from the ship to Anchorage. Arrival-city costs are not captured yet.
routeFamilies.bestFor: The most glaciers in seven nights
routeFamilies.textBasis: Planner summary written in P6 from the catalog and line notes; general knowledge, not a sourced figure.

routeFamilies.name: One way Seward/Whittier to Vancouver
routeFamilies.why: The same idea in reverse: start near Anchorage (Seward or Whittier) and finish in Vancouver, usually with Hubbard Glacier early in the week.
routeFamilies.tradeoff: Fly into Anchorage and home from Vancouver, plus the transfer from Anchorage to the ship. Arrival-city costs are not captured yet.
routeFamilies.bestFor: Adding Anchorage or Denali before the cruise
routeFamilies.textBasis: Planner summary written in P6 from the catalog and line notes; general knowledge, not a sourced figure.

lines.accessibility: Accessible staterooms bookable on the line's site (check 'Accessible stateroom').
lines.alaskaNotes: Alaska specialist: sailing Alaska since 1969 and the biggest Glacier Bay presence (85 Glacier Bay calls planned in 2027). Owns five wilderness lodges (incl. Denali and Mt. McKinley Princess) for cruisetours. Glacier Bay on most Seattle and Vancouver itineraries here; Voyage of the Glaciers one-ways add College Fjord or Hubbard.

lines.name: Holland America Line
lines.fareBasis: Standard fare shown with 'All taxes and fees included'. 'Have It All' package is an optional add-on.
lines.includes: Main dining, Lido buffet, live music venues, 24-hour room service. Drinks, Wi-Fi and gratuities extra on the base fare.

payment.note: Sources disagree (75 vs 90 days). Confirm at booking.

lines.accessibility: Booking flow has a 'Wheelchair Accessible Room' checkbox.
lines.alaskaNotes: Alaska specialist: 80 years in Alaska in 2027. Holds Glacier Bay permits (Eurodam Seattle Explorer and Glacier Discovery one-ways); a National Park ranger boards for the Glacier Bay day. Owns Holland America Denali Lodge for cruisetours; 'Glacier Guarantee' and Alaska Up Close talks aboard. Many summer Vancouver sailings are sold only as cruisetours.

lines.name: Norwegian Cruise Line
lines.fareBasis: Base fare ('Free at Sea' / More at Sea extras optional). Joy sailings showed a 'Black Friday Latitudes Sale' price to logged-out visitors.
lines.includes: Main dining rooms, buffet, Broadway-style shows. Freestyle dining (no fixed times). Drinks, Wi-Fi and service charge extra on the base fare.

payment.deposit: $250 per person for 7+ day sailings (secondary source).
payment.note: Verify in NCL Guest Ticket Contract.

lines.accessibility: 'I need an accessible stateroom' option in booking; requires affirmation of need.
lines.alaskaNotes: Holds Glacier Bay entry: Norwegian Jade's northbound Vancouver-Whittier sailings and some Joy 9-day Seattle trips include it. Sells Denali cruisetours around Jade's one-ways (Anchorage/Fairbanks Denali Express, Denali by Rail, etc. seen on ncl.com). Big resort-style ships; freestyle dining.

lines.name: Royal Caribbean
lines.fareBasis: Price shown with 'all taxes & fees'. Page also tagged '10% Off Resident Rate' and 'Early Booking Bonus'; no residency discount was applied.
lines.includes: Main dining, Windjammer buffet, shows, pools. Drinks, Wi-Fi and gratuities extra.

payment.deposit: Refundable and non-refundable deposit fares; non-refundable fares become a cruise credit minus $100 pp if cancelled before final payment.

lines.accessibility: Accessible staterooms available by request in booking.
lines.alaskaNotes: No Glacier Bay permit (not on the NPS-authorized list); glacier days are Dawes/Endicott Arm, Tracy Arm or Hubbard. Big-ship activities (rock walls, North Star on Quantum-class). Anthem's Seward one-ways reach Hubbard Glacier.

lines.name: Celebrity Cruises
lines.fareBasis: Price shown with 'all taxes & fees' and the '75% Off 2nd Guest' promotion. Default fare type (cruise-only vs All Included) not confirmed.
lines.includes: Main dining, buffet, shows. All Included upgrade adds drinks, Wi-Fi and tips.

payment.note: Taken from Celebrity's UK FAQ; confirm US terms.

lines.accessibility: Inside staterooms listed as including accessible options.
lines.alaskaNotes: No Glacier Bay permit; glacier days are Dawes/Endicott Arm or Hubbard. More upscale feel than Royal Caribbean (same parent company); Solstice one-ways to Seward add Hubbard Glacier.

lines.name: Carnival Cruise Line
lines.fareBasis: Public fare for 2 adults, no military/senior/past-guest discounts, 'Taxes and fees are included'.
lines.includes: Main dining, Lido buffet, comedy and shows. Drinks, Wi-Fi and gratuities extra.
lines.alaskaNotes: No Glacier Bay permit; the Seattle itinerary here uses Tracy Arm. Lowest fares and the most casual atmosphere; a single ship (Carnival Legend) does the Seattle run.

lines.name: MSC Cruises
lines.fareBasis: 'Price includes all fees and taxes' for 2 guests. A '10% off with Voyagers Club' member discount was shown but not applied.
lines.includes: Main dining, buffet, shows. Drinks and Wi-Fi extra unless a package is added.
lines.alaskaNotes: No Glacier Bay permit. Newer to Alaska (Seattle round trips); glacier day is Dawes/Endicott or Tracy Arm per itinerary.

lines.name: Virgin Voyages
lines.fareBasis: Adults-only (18+). 'Black Friday Preview: 80% off 2nd Sailor' pricing shown per sailor.
lines.includes: All restaurants (no buffet), gratuities, basic drinks, Wi-Fi.
lines.alaskaNotes: No Glacier Bay permit. Adults-only (18+), so a family of four adults qualifies. Newer to Alaska.

lines.name: Oceania Cruises
lines.fareBasis: Premium line; adults-only since Jan 2026 per European agent listing. Prices here are aggregator samples only.
lines.includes: Specialty dining included; small ship (about 1,250 guests).
lines.alaskaNotes: No Glacier Bay permit. Premium small-ish ships (about 1,250 guests); adults-only per an agent listing. Seattle round trips start late June.

lines.name: Disney Cruise Line
lines.fareBasis: Family-focused line. Alaska sailings 2027 are round trips from Vancouver only (Disney Wonder Mondays, Disney Magic Thursdays). Prices here are reseller 'from' samples; Disney's own search could not be read.
lines.includes: Rotational dining (three main restaurants in turn), Broadway-style Disney shows, soft drinks at meals and drink stations. Alcohol, Wi-Fi, adult-only dining and gratuities extra.
lines.alaskaNotes: No Glacier Bay permit; the glacier day is scenic viewing at the Stikine Icecap. Family-focused line sailing only from Vancouver in Alaska. Disney's own search page could not be read on 2026-11-07, so prices here are reseller samples.

places.name: Smith Cove Cruise Terminal (Pier 91)
places.notes: Interbay/Magnolia, about 3 mi north of downtown. Used by Princess, Holland America, Royal Caribbean, Celebrity, Carnival, MSC and Virgin (typical assignment; confirm on cruise documents). Taxi/rideshare or cruise-line transfer to SEA airport, roughly 30-45 min.

places.name: Bell Street Cruise Terminal (Pier 66)
places.notes: Downtown waterfront in Belltown, near Pike Place Market. Used by Norwegian and Oceania (typical assignment; confirm). Downtown hotels are a short ride away.

places.name: Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA)
places.notes: Arrival/departure airport for the ABQ flights (Phase 3).

places.name: Juneau, Alaska

photo2.credit: Mark Hogan / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 2.0

places.notes: Ships normally berth at the downtown docks; the Mount Roberts Tramway base is on the waterfront. Mendenhall Glacier is about 12 miles away (bus or tour needed). Busiest port in Southeast Alaska: several ships a day in June.

logistics.text: Goldbelt Tram base station is on the cruise docks at 490 S. Franklin St. (tram closed in 2026; 2027 reopening unconfirmed).
Mendenhall Visitor Center is reached from its parking lots by stairs, elevators and an easy ramp.
Allen Marine's Juneau office is in Auke Bay (13391 Glacier Highway). Cruise whale tours include a motorcoach from downtown.
Franklin Dock and the cruise terminal are a few minutes' walk to downtown and fully wheelchair accessible; AJ Dock is about 1 mile south of the center with a $5 shuttle.
Capital Transit routes 3, 4 and 8 stop at Dredge Lake Road, about 1.5 miles (30 minutes' flat paved walk) from the Mendenhall visitor center; $2 adult fare, up to about 1.5 hours each way.
Mendenhall paths: 1/3 mile paved round trip; Nugget Falls gravel trail about 2 miles round trip on the Forest Service map.
No 2027 reopening date for the Goldbelt tram as of 2026-11-07; it needs a state certification evaluation first.

places.name: Skagway, Alaska

photo2.credit: Diego Delso / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

places.notes: Docks are at the south end of town; Broadway's historic district starts within roughly half a mile. White Pass & Yukon Route trains board near the docks. Flat, compact town; Canada (Yukon) excursions need passports.

logistics.text: Frontier Excursions' default pickup is at the cruise pier where it meets land outside the security gates (or 3rd and Broadway).
No fee to enter Klondike Gold Rush NHP; ranger programs and museums are free.
SMART bus runs dock to downtown 7 am to 9 pm on ship days ($3 each way, $5 all day); on-demand shuttle to the River Bridge ($5), Dyea Road pavement end ($10) and Dyea ($15).
Under a mile (about 18 minutes) from the ships to downtown; Broadway Dock at the edge of Broadway, Railroad and Ore docks at the south end of town; all piers wheelchair accessible.

Rental companies listed by the visitor bureau: Affordable Car Rentals (648 Broadway) and Drive About (202 9th Ave). Canada-driving rules were not found in writing; cruisers say US citizens can cross with passports.

places.name: Ketchikan, Alaska (downtown)
places.notes: Downtown berths put Creek Street and the waterfront a short, flat walk from the gangway. Often rainy: Ketchikan is one of the wettest towns in the US.

logistics.text: Alaska Rainforest Sanctuary is at Herring Cove, about 8 road miles from town.
Four downtown berths (1 to 4, south to north) put the ship on Front Street; Saxman is about 2 miles south, Totem Bight a few miles north.
Totem Heritage Center is about a 15-minute walk from downtown; Creek Street's boardwalk is flat but slippery when wet.
Borough bus to Totem Bight takes about 25 minutes and runs roughly hourly (May 2023 timetable); $2 cash fare, whole fleet wheelchair accessible.

places.name: Ketchikan – Ward Cove
places.notes: Norwegian's Ketchikan calls use the Ward Cove dock about 7 miles north of downtown; reaching Creek Street needs a shuttle or taxi (allow 20-30 min each way). Adds a transfer for the parents.

logistics.text: A reseller lists a Ward Cove to downtown shuttle at $65 (one way, per-person basis unclear).
From the Ward Cove bus stop, Totem Bight is about 5 minutes and 3 miles by borough bus (May 2023 blog).

places.name: Sitka, Alaska
places.notes: Most large ships use the Sitka Sound Cruise Terminal several miles north of downtown with a shuttle into town; some calls tender to downtown instead. Dock vs tender is set per call, so confirm closer to sailing.
places.dock: Dock north of town with shuttle, or tender

logistics.text: Alaska Raptor Center: 1000 Raptor Way; adult admission $17 in person; spring/summer 8 am to 4 pm.
Sitka National Historical Park has no entrance fee.

places.name: Icy Strait Point (Hoonah), Alaska
places.notes: Tlingit-owned destination built around a restored 1912 cannery near the village of Hoonah. Ships dock at the cannery complex; whale watching departs nearby; gondolas and the ZipRider are on site.

logistics.text: ZipRider reservations generally must be made through the cruise line; ride is 5,495 ft over about 90 seconds.

places.name: Victoria, British Columbia
places.notes: Ships berth at Ogden Point, roughly 1.5-2 km from the Inner Harbour. Most Seattle round trips call in the evening for a few hours (required foreign-port stop). Canada: bring passports.

places.name: Glacier Bay National Park

photo2.credit: Betty Wills (Atsme) / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

places.notes: National Park Service limits ship entries; park rangers board for commentary. Ship cruises up to tidewater glaciers such as Margerie and Johns Hopkins (ice permitting). No going ashore.

places.name: Tracy Arm Fjord
places.notes: Narrow fjord south of Juneau ending at the Sawyer Glaciers. Large ships often cannot reach the glacier faces when ice is heavy; lines may substitute Endicott Arm.

places.name: Endicott Arm & Dawes Glacier

photo2.credit: Larry Syverson / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 2.0

places.notes: Fjord next to Tracy Arm, ending at Dawes Glacier. Usually a morning scenic cruise before an afternoon Juneau call.

places.name: Hubbard Glacier
places.notes: North America's largest tidewater glacier (about 6 miles wide at the face), in Disenchantment Bay near Yakutat. Rare on 7-night Seattle round trips.

places.name: Stephens Passage
places.notes: Channel south of Juneau, known for humpback whales. Holland America lists it as scenic cruising on the way in to Juneau.

places.name: Canada Place cruise terminal, Vancouver
places.notes: Downtown Vancouver waterfront, next to Waterfront SkyTrain station. US-bound ships clear US border pre-clearance here before boarding. Canada Line SkyTrain runs from YVR airport to Waterfront (about 26 min).

places.name: Whittier, Alaska (cruise port for Anchorage)
places.notes: Small port about 60 mi by road from Anchorage. Road access is only through the one-lane Anton Anderson tunnel, which runs on a fixed schedule; rail also connects to Anchorage. Princess, Holland America and others use it for one-way Gulf of Alaska cruises.

places.name: College Fjord, Alaska
places.notes: Fjord in northern Prince William Sound lined with tidewater and valley glaciers named after colleges. Ships cruise it in the evening before arriving in Whittier.

places.name: Seward, Alaska (cruise port for Anchorage)
places.notes: Resurrection Bay port about 125 mi (2.5-3 h) by road from Anchorage; the Alaska Railroad also runs Seward-Anchorage in summer. Used by Royal Caribbean, Celebrity, Norwegian and luxury lines for one-way Gulf of Alaska cruises.

places.name: Prince Rupert, British Columbia
places.notes: Small northern BC port (Northland cruise terminal is downtown). Canadian port: passports needed.

places.name: Inside Passage (British Columbia), scenic cruising
places.notes: Sheltered coastal channels between Vancouver Island and the mainland; ships list a scenic-cruising day with no landing.

places.name: Haines, Alaska
places.notes: Small town on Lynn Canal, about 15 mi by water south of Skagway. Quieter than Skagway; known for bald eagles (Chilkat preserve). Port Chilkoot dock is a short walk from town.

places.name: Stikine Icecap (scenic glacier viewing)
places.notes: Large icefield on the Alaska-BC border east of Petersburg and Wrangell. Disney lists a scenic glacier-viewing day here; which glacier face the ship approaches is not stated.

pois.name: Auke Bay harbor (whale boats)
pois.note: Most Juneau whale tours leave from here, about 12 mi from the cruise docks by coach.

pois.name: Mendenhall Glacier Visitor Center
pois.note: About 12-13 mi from the docks. The Wikipedia glacier coordinates (58.4958, -134.5322) are up-glacier; the pin is at the visitor center.

pois.name: Juneau helicopter bases (airport area)
pois.note: Glacier-landing helicopters fly from near Juneau airport; exact base depends on the operator.

pois.name: Goldbelt (Mount Roberts) Tram base
pois.note: On the cruise docks at 490 S. Franklin St. Closed in 2026; 2027 reopening unconfirmed.

pois.name: White Pass summit (train turnaround)
pois.note: About 20 rail miles from Skagway; the summit train turns around here.

pois.name: Carcross, Yukon (bus and rail tours)
pois.note: Longer Yukon tours reach Carcross; Canadian border crossing (bring passports).

pois.name: Klondike Gold Rush NHP visitor center
pois.note: Broadway & 2nd Ave, a short walk from the cruise docks.

pois.name: Creek Street
pois.note: Historic boardwalk a short walk from the downtown docks.

pois.name: Totem Bight State Historical Park
pois.note: About 10 mi north of downtown; short gravel trail to the totems and clan house.

pois.name: Misty Fjords National Monument
pois.note: Reached by boat (about 5 h round trip) or floatplane.

pois.name: Alaska Raptor Center
pois.note: 1000 Raptor Way, about 1 mi from downtown Sitka.

pois.name: Sitka National Historical Park (totem trail)
pois.note: Flat, mostly gravel trail; no entrance fee.

pois.name: Victoria Inner Harbour
pois.note: About 1.5 mi from the Ogden Point cruise terminal.

pois.name: Butchart Gardens
pois.note: About 13 mi from the cruise terminal; tours run on evening calls in summer.

linesReviewed.line: Small-ship and expedition lines (UnCruise, Lindblad, Alaskan Dream, American Cruise Lines)
linesReviewed.finding: Ships of roughly 50-150 guests sailing from Juneau, Sitka or Ketchikan (not Seattle/Vancouver), with kayaks, skiffs and naturalists instead of shows. Prices are far higher: roughly 5 to 10 times a big-ship interior fare per person for a summer week (UnCruise and Lindblad samples in notes/phase1.md). Fit for the parents is mixed: most days include shore landings by small boat and wet-step or beach landings, and several of these ships have no elevator. Good fit for the brothers; check each ship's accessibility page before considering it for the parents. Alaskan Dream Cruises and American Cruise Lines were not priced.
